cleanIntro: The Midsize is a shorter-gripped, 4-inch-barrel 509 on its own frame, with its own backstraps and its own 15-round magazine — the parts list gives it a Midsize Frame column and the specification table gives it a line of its own. The takedown is the series procedure: lever a hundred degrees clockwise, striker released deliberately, slide forward off the frame.

steps.title: Check the name on the slide says 509, and that yours is the Midsize
steps.action: Read the model designation on the slide. The specification table in this book carries a separate line for the FN 509 MIDSIZE — 4-inch barrel, 7.4 inches long, 5.2 inches tall, 26.5 ounces, 15-round standard magazine — so compare those against your pistol. If it does not carry 509 in its name, get the FN manual written for the pistol you have.
steps.prose: Knowing you are on the Midsize line matters mostly for the parts you handle afterwards: FN lists Midsize backstraps and 509M magazines separately from the full-size ones, and the Compact shares neither. Nothing in the strip changes between frame sizes, but a Compact backstrap will not go on a Midsize frame and a Compact magazine is a different body. Settle it now, at the bench, rather than when a part refuses to seat.
steps.aside: FN's scope line for the whole book: IF YOUR FN PISTOL DOES NOT HAVE 509 IN ITS NAMING CONVENTION OR IF THE APPEARANCE OF THE PISTOL DOES NOT CORRESPOND TO THE ILLUSTRATIONS IN THIS OWNER’S MANUAL CONTACT YOUR DEALER, DEPARTMENT ARMORER OR CONTACT FN DIRECTLY TO OBTAIN THE OWNER’S MANUAL THAT HAS BEEN WRITTEN SPECIFICALLY FOR YOUR PISTOL.
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §15 Technical specs, model column, p.72

steps.title: Magazine out, and expect it to sit deep in a short grip
steps.action: Muzzle safe, finger clear of the trigger, press the magazine release and remove the magazine. If it does not drop free, pull down on the base plate while holding the release in.
steps.prose: The Midsize grip is short enough that a flush 15-round magazine leaves very little base plate to grab, so this is the 509 where a sticky magazine most often needs the pull FN describes. If yours has an extended 17- or 24-round magazine fitted there is plenty to hold, but there is also more weight bearing on the catch. Get it fully out of the well before anything else moves.
steps.quote: Press the magazine release and remove the magazine. If the magazine does not drop out of the pistol, pull on the magazine base plate while pressing the magazine release (Figure 12).
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §6.3 Unloading, step 1, p.22
steps.warn: Magazine before chamber. Cycling the slide with a loaded magazine seated just feeds the pistol again.

steps.title: Eject the chamber and lock the slide open
steps.action: Pull the slide fully rearward to eject any chambered round, then press the slide stop up and let the slide rest against it, held open.
steps.prose: The Midsize slide is shorter than the full-size and the recoil spring is no lighter, so it gives less stroke to build momentum — pull it decisively to the stop rather than easing it. A short pull that drags a round part way out and lets it fall back into the chamber is exactly how a pistol gets called clear when it is not. Both slide stop levers work, so use whichever thumb reaches.
steps.quote: Lock the slide to the rear by pressing the slide stop up and allowing the slide to rest against the slide stop retaining it to the rear (Figure 13).
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §6.3 Unloading, step 2, p.22

steps.title: Look into the chamber and the magazine well
steps.action: With the slide locked open, look into the ejection port at the chamber and down through the magazine well, and confirm by eye that both are empty.
steps.prose: The 509's loaded chamber indicator is the extractor lifting to show a red dot on the right of the slide, plus a wide groove you can feel at the front of the rear serrations. That tells you when there is a case in there; it is not a way to establish there is not. This is the check that licenses the trigger press later in the strip, so it is worth doing twice.
steps.quote: Inspect the chamber and magazine well to ensure no cartridge is present. Remember, merely removing the magazine does not mean the chamber is unloaded (Figure 14).
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §6.3 Unloading, step 3, p.22
steps.warn: THE RED DOT THAT INDICATES A LOADED CHAMBER CAN BECOME OBSCURED. DO NOT DEPEND ON THE RED INDICATOR TO DETERMINE THE UNLOADED CONDITION OF THE PISTOL.

steps.title: Does this Midsize have the manual safety?
steps.action: Look at the rear of the frame above the grip for a small lever on each side. If it is there, push it down to the fire position before disassembly; if not, your pistol has no manual safety and there is nothing here to set.
steps.prose: FN offers the 509 with and without and heads the section with an explicit qualifier, so the book will not decide it for you. It is load-bearing in this strip: the safety blocks the sear carrier and trigger assembly, so with it engaged the deliberate striker release simply will not happen and the slide stays locked to the frame. FN also states the safety cannot be engaged with the trigger held rearward, so it is not something to reach for once the strip is under way.
steps.quote: 9.2 MANUAL SAFETY (APPLICABLE ONLY TO PISTOLS WITH A MANUAL SAFETY)
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §9.2 heading, p.30

steps.title: Threaded muzzle? Take the protector off before the lever
steps.action: Look at the muzzle of the 4-inch barrel. If it is threaded, unscrew the thread protector or muzzle device counterclockwise and set it aside now.
steps.prose: FN qualifies its threaded-barrel section because only some 509s carry it, and on a Midsize the threading takes up a real fraction of an already short barrel — leave a device on and it fouls the slide's forward travel as it comes off the frame. The threads are ½"-28 and the protector is meant to be fitted whenever nothing else is. If your muzzle is plain, this step is not yours; go to the lever.
steps.aside: FN's qualifier: 9.8 THREADED BARREL (APPLICABLE ONLY TO PISTOLS WITH THREADED BARRELS).
steps.quote: Remove the thread protector or muzzle device if the pistol is equipped with a threaded barrel (Figure 40).
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §11.1 Field strip, step 3, p.36

steps.title: Takedown lever a hundred degrees clockwise
steps.action: With the slide still locked to the rear, rotate the takedown lever roughly 100 degrees clockwise until it comes to a stop.
steps.prose: Past square, not at it — the lever needs the full hundred degrees or the slide will not release, and "nearly there" feels identical to jammed. The slide has to remain locked open while you turn it; if it has crept forward, put it back on the stop rather than forcing the lever. On the Midsize there is less frame in front of your fingers, so brace the pistol on the bench rather than gripping it around the dust cover.
steps.quote: Rotate the takedown lever approximately 100 deg. clockwise (Figure 41).
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §11.1 Field strip, step 4, p.36

steps.title: Release the striker with the rear faces in line
steps.action: Hold the slide, release it off the slide stop and ease it forward. Keep the rear of the slide level with the rear of the frame, point the muzzle in a safe direction, and press the trigger to drop the striker. The slide creeps forward slightly as it releases.
steps.prose: FN prints a warning against this step precisely because it is a trigger press on a pistol you have just declared empty — which is why the chamber was checked by eye a moment ago. The alignment is what makes it work: let the slide run all the way forward first and the sear recaptures the striker, and then nothing comes apart. If that happens, bring the slide back into line and repeat rather than pulling harder.
steps.quote: While keeping the rear of the slide and rear of the frame in alignment, point the muzzle in a safe direction and press the trigger to release the striker. The slide will move forward slightly when released (Figure 43).
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §11.1 Field strip, step 5, p.37
steps.warn: THE PISTOL MUST BE COMPLETELY UNLOADED TO PERFORM STEP 5. FAILURE TO FOLLOW THIS WARNING COULD RESULT IN SERIOUS INJURY OR DEATH.

steps.title: Slide forward and off
steps.action: With the striker down, run the slide forward off the frame rails and lift it away as one assembly with the barrel and recoil spring inside.
steps.prose: No force should be needed. If it stops at the front of the rails, either the striker recocked or the takedown lever has turned back — check both instead of pulling, because the rails are the one pair of bearing surfaces on this pistol you cannot buy back. Support the slide as it frees; the recoil spring inside is still under compression against the barrel lug.
steps.quote: After releasing the striker, you can remove the slide by pulling the slide forward and away from the frame.
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §11.1 Field strip, step 6, p.37

steps.title: Recoil spring assembly out by its small spring
steps.action: Turn the slide upside down, take hold of the small spring at the front of the recoil spring assembly, lift that end up out of its recess and draw the assembly clear.
steps.prose: The Midsize uses the same captive arrangement in a shorter slide, so the spring stack is stiffer for its length and wants to be released rather than fought — grasp the small forward spring so the lift takes the load off. It should come out in one movement with no tools. Keep the assembly together; FN treats a separated guide rod as an armorer's problem, not a cleaning one.
steps.quote: Hold the slide upside down, grasp the small spring of the recoil spring assembly then lift the recoil spring assembly up and out of the slide (Figure 45).
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §11.1 Field strip, step 7, p.38

steps.title: Barrel up, around the extractor, rearward out
steps.action: Grip the 4-inch barrel by the lug beneath it, lift it up, take it around the extractor and slide it rearward out of the slide.
steps.prose: Lift, swing, then back — in that order. The shorter barrel gives you less to hold and tempts a straight rearward pull, and a straight pull with the lug still seated drives the barrel hood into the extractor claw. That claw is a sprung part with a job to do on every shot, so it is worth the extra second. With the barrel out the strip is finished.
steps.quote: Grasp the barrel by its lug, lift it up and around the extractor and slide the barrel rearward out of the slide (Figure 46).
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §11.1 Field strip, step 9, p.38

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Midsize frame, slide, 4-inch barrel and recoil spring assembly on the bench — with the thread protector too if yours is threaded. FN calls that sufficient for a thorough clean and sends anything deeper to a qualified armorer.
steps.prose: That opens up everything the cleaning section asks for: bore and chamber from the breech end, breech face and extractor, both slide rails, the barrel's unlock surface and the magazine well. FN's interval is after every use, or every 500 rounds under intensive shooting, and sooner for salt, sand, moisture, dirty ammunition or suppressor use. Deep Clean covers the Midsize magazine, the Midsize backstraps and the optics plate.
steps.quote: This level of disassembly is sufficient to perform a thorough cleaning. Disassembly beyond the instructions provided in this manual should only be carried out by a qualified armorer.
steps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §11.1 Field strip, closing note, p.38

deepSteps.title: Strip the 509M magazine, spring capped
deepSteps.action: Confirm the magazine is empty. Point its base away from you, press the floor plate catch in through the hole in the floor plate, slide the plate forward off the body with your palm over the spring, then take out the catch, spring and follower.
deepSteps.prose: The Midsize's standard magazine is 15 rounds and the parts list catalogues 509M bodies at 15, 17 and 24 — all with the same floor plate catch under real spring load. Cap the base with your hand before the plate starts to move, then bleed the tension off gradually rather than letting the plate fly. On rebuild the follower angle has to match the feed lip angle, and the catch tab must be visible standing through the floor plate before the magazine goes back in.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the floor plate catch, magazine spring and follower from the magazine body (Figure 60).
deepSteps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §11.4 Magazine disassembly, step 2, p.43
deepSteps.warn: CAUTION: THE MAGAZINE SPRING IS UNDER TENSION. WEAR EYE PROTECTION AND KEEP THE BOTTOM OF THE MAGAZINE POINTED IN A SAFE DIRECTION.

deepSteps.title: Which magazines belong in a Midsize
deepSteps.action: Sort your magazines before you strip them. Bigger 509 magazines of the same caliber will run in a pistol that takes smaller ones, so a full-size 17 or 24 will feed a Midsize with the base plate standing proud — but any 509 magazine this manual does not describe should have come with its own addendum, and without one you ask FN rather than guessing.
deepSteps.prose: This is the compatibility rule that actually bites at the bench: the Midsize will run a longer magazine, but the parts and the disassembly may not match the drawings in this book. FN also notes 509 magazines will function in older FNS pistols with the base plate misaligned, and that FNS magazines can be used in a 509 if their base plates are replaced — useful to know and not an invitation to mix floor plates between patterns.
deepSteps.aside: FN's own limit on the book's scope: FN 509 magazines not specifically covered in this manual should be covered by an addendum included with this manual or with the magazine.
deepSteps.quote: Larger capacity FN 509 magazines will function in FN 509 pistols capable of accepting smaller capacity magazines of the same caliber.
deepSteps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §9.6 Magazine, p.33

deepSteps.title: Midsize backstrap off, 5/64" roll pin punch
deepSteps.action: With the frame stripped and confirmed empty, drive the backstrap retaining pin out with a small 5/64" roll pin punch, then slide the backstrap off the rear dovetail.
deepSteps.prose: The pin is a roll pin and a solid punch will crush it, after which nothing holds the strap. FN lists the Midsize backstraps under their own part numbers in the frame assembly section, small, medium and large, so this is also the moment to check you are refitting a Midsize strap and not a full-size one. Refitting, press the strap in until the gap at the top closes and line its hole up with the dovetail slot before the pin goes back.
deepSteps.quote: Using a small 5/64" roll pin punch, push out the backstrap
deepSteps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §11.3 Backstrap removal, step 1, p.41

deepSteps.title: Optic cut: clean dry, and keep threadlocker away
deepSteps.action: If your Midsize is an MRD and you are cleaning under the optic or slide cap, remove the two screws counterclockwise, lift off the optic, MRD plate and o-ring, clean the mounting surface, and rebuild with the screws and holes free of lubricant, the o-ring in its recess and the screws tightened by finger pressure with the T10 Torx.
deepSteps.prose: FN's mounting system is self-locking by design, and threadlocker on it can make the optic impossible to remove later without damaging the components. Oil is the opposite hazard — a lubricated screw thread lets the fasteners loosen under recoil. Clean, dry, o-ring sandwiched between slide and plate, and confirm the zero afterwards, because FN says zeroing has to be rechecked every time the optic comes off.
deepSteps.cite: FN 509® Series AUTOLOADING PISTOL OWNER'S MANUAL — 2603-FN 509-OM 66-100498 — §11.5 Optics mounting system, note, p.47

cleaning.name: BARREL & BORE
tasks: Solvent into the bore and chamber of the 4-inch barrel, a few minutes to soak, then patches on a rod from the chamber end only
Never clean from the muzzle — FN warns that damaging the muzzle affects accuracy, and on a short barrel there is less bore to forgive it
Patch until they come out clean, then one patch with preservative oil to leave a protective film
A light film of gun oil on the outside of the barrel and its unlock surface

cleaning.name: SLIDE, FRAME & RAILS
tasks: Brush and solvent on the breech face, under the extractor and around the ejection port
Wipe both slide rails and put a drop of lightweight oil on each, along with the striker block, sear, disconnect cam, cartridge guide and unlock block from FN's lubrication figure
Soft cloth down the magazine well of the Midsize frame to clear lint and debris; keep solvent off the polymer
Inspect the stripped parts for wear or damage while they are apart, and ask FN about anything that looks wrong rather than reassembling it

cleaning.name: INTERVAL & STORAGE
tasks: Never soak the pistol in solvent or lubricant, and keep the oil sparing — excess interferes with function
Clean and lubricate after every use; in intensive shooting FN's outside limit is every 500 rounds
Weather, salt, sand, moisture, dirty ammunition or suppressor use all pull that interval in — a carried Midsize earns a wipe-down more often than a range gun
Wipe the exterior free of fingerprints and excess oil, and dry-patch the bore before the pistol is fired again

reassembly: Barrel into the slide first: muzzle out through the barrel hole from the inside, let it drop, then back to the breech face until the lug locks.
Thread protector or muzzle device back on clockwise if this Midsize has a threaded barrel.
Large end of the recoil spring assembly against the recess at the front of the slide, compressed, its rear centred on the barrel lug.
Slide and barrel onto the frame rails, run fully rearward and locked on the slide stop.
Takedown lever rotated upward to lock frame and slide together, then release the slide forward.
Test slide stop, trigger, magazine release and the manual safety if fitted, with an empty magazine, before anything is loaded.
fncheck: Empty and back together: the takedown lever should sit flush and refuse to rotate with the slide closed; the slide should go fully into battery on its own spring and lock back on either ambidextrous stop; the trigger should reset with a click as the slide cycles; an empty 15-round 509M magazine should drop clear of the short grip when the release is pressed, and a longer 17 or 24 should seat and drop the same way; and if your Midsize carries the manual safety, both levers should snap into position on their detent — noting FN's warning that the safety cannot be engaged with the trigger held to the rear.
